meta.note: Dates are YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. 'to': null means still true on the end date. 'check' marks a claim to verify. 'src' is the source that supports the item.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.bio: Runs Tesla and SpaceX. Co-chaired OpenAI 2015–2018. Founded xAI in 2023; SpaceX bought it in 2026.

people.name: Sam Altman
people.bio: President of Y Combinator 2014–2019. OpenAI co-founder; CEO since 2019.

people.name: Greg Brockman
people.bio: Former Stripe CTO. OpenAI co-founder and president.

people.name: Ilya Sutskever
people.bio: Co-created AlexNet with Alex Krizhevsky and Hinton. OpenAI co-founder; its chief scientist until 2024. Co-founded Safe Superintelligence in 2024; its CEO since 2025.

people.name: Andrej Karpathy
people.bio: OpenAI founding member. Led Tesla's AI team 2017–2022. Founded Eureka Labs in 2024. Joined Anthropic in 2026.

people.name: John Schulman
people.bio: OpenAI co-founder who co-led the post-training team behind ChatGPT. Moved to Anthropic in 2024, then Thinking Machines.

people.name: Mira Murati
people.bio: Worked on the Model X at Tesla. OpenAI CTO, briefly interim CEO. Founded Thinking Machines Lab in 2025.

people.name: Dario Amodei
people.bio: Led research at OpenAI, including GPT-2 and GPT-3. Left in 2020 to co-found Anthropic; its CEO.

people.name: Daniela Amodei
people.bio: Ran safety and policy at OpenAI. Co-founder and president of Anthropic.

people.name: Jack Clark
people.bio: OpenAI's policy director. Co-founded Anthropic and led its policy work.

people.name: Chris Olah
people.bio: Interpretability researcher at Google Brain and OpenAI. Anthropic co-founder.

people.name: Tom Brown
people.bio: Lead author of the GPT-3 paper at OpenAI. Anthropic co-founder.

people.name: Jared Kaplan
people.bio: Physicist who co-wrote OpenAI's scaling-laws paper. Anthropic co-founder and chief science officer.

people.name: Jan Leike
people.bio: Safety researcher at DeepMind, then co-led OpenAI's superalignment team. Joined Anthropic in 2024.

people.name: Demis Hassabis
people.bio: DeepMind co-founder. Its CEO until August 2026; now its chair and Alphabet's chief scientist. Shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold.

people.name: Shane Legg
people.bio: DeepMind co-founder and chief AGI scientist.

people.name: Mustafa Suleyman
people.bio: DeepMind co-founder. Co-founded Inflection AI in 2022. CEO of Microsoft AI since 2024.

people.name: Larry Page
people.bio: Google co-founder. Google CEO, then Alphabet CEO until 2019. Reportedly led the DeepMind purchase.

people.name: Sergey Brin
people.bio: Google co-founder. Came back to work on Gemini in 2023.

people.name: Sundar Pichai
people.bio: Google CEO since 2015 and Alphabet CEO since 2019.

people.name: Geoffrey Hinton
people.bio: Deep-learning pioneer. At Google 2013–2023, then left to warn about AI risk. 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics.

people.name: Noam Shazeer
people.bio: Co-author of the Transformer paper. Co-founded Character.AI and returned to Google in 2024. Left for OpenAI in 2026.

people.name: Yann LeCun
people.bio: Founded Facebook AI Research in 2013. Meta's chief AI scientist until 2025, then co-founded AMI Labs.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.bio: Founder and CEO of Facebook, renamed Meta in 2021.

people.name: Alexandr Wang
people.bio: Co-founded Scale AI in 2016. Meta's chief AI officer since 2025.

people.name: Nat Friedman
people.bio: Former GitHub CEO and AI investor with Daniel Gross. Joined Meta's superintelligence lab in 2025.

people.name: Daniel Gross
people.bio: Investor; co-founded Safe Superintelligence with Sutskever. Left for Meta in 2025.

people.name: Satya Nadella
people.bio: Microsoft CEO since 2014. Struck the OpenAI partnership in 2019.

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.bio: Nvidia co-founder and CEO. Supplies the chips most AI labs train on.

people.name: Peter Thiel
people.bio: PayPal co-founder with Musk. Early backer of DeepMind and OpenAI.

people.name: Reid Hoffman
people.bio: PayPal executive, LinkedIn co-founder. Early OpenAI donor and board member. Co-founded Inflection AI.

people.name: Jaan Tallinn
people.bio: Skype co-founder. Early DeepMind investor. Led Anthropic's first funding round.

people.name: Sam Bankman-Fried
people.bio: FTX founder. Led Anthropic's 2022 round, months before FTX collapsed.

people.name: Helen Toner
people.bio: OpenAI board member 2021–2023. Voted to remove Altman.

people.name: Adam D'Angelo
people.bio: Quora CEO. On OpenAI's board since 2018; the one member kept after November 2023.

people.name: Shivon Zilis
people.bio: Neuralink executive and long-time Musk adviser. On OpenAI's board 2020–2023.

people.name: Igor Babuschkin
people.bio: Researcher at DeepMind and OpenAI. Co-founded xAI in 2023; left in 2025 to start an AI safety fund.

people.name: Arthur Mensch
people.bio: DeepMind researcher. Co-founded Mistral AI in 2023; its CEO.

people.name: Liang Wenfeng
people.bio: Hedge-fund founder who started DeepSeek in 2023.

people.name: Masayoshi Son
people.bio: SoftBank founder. Chairs Stargate and became one of OpenAI's largest investors.

people.name: Larry Ellison
people.bio: Oracle co-founder. Close Musk friend; on Tesla's board 2018–2022. Stargate partner.

people.name: Donald Trump
people.bio: US President 2017–2021 and again from January 2025. Launched Stargate at the White House.

people.name: Barret Zoph
people.bio: Former OpenAI research vice president. Co-founded Thinking Machines in 2025. Rejoined OpenAI in 2026, then moved to Google DeepMind.

people.name: Clément Delangue
people.bio: French entrepreneur. Co-founded Hugging Face in 2016; its CEO.

people.name: Julien Chaumond
people.bio: French engineer. Co-founded Hugging Face in 2016; its CTO.

people.name: Thomas Wolf
people.bio: Physicist turned AI researcher. Co-founded Hugging Face in 2016 and leads its science work.

orgs.name: Google
orgs.bio: Search giant; parent company Alphabet from 2015.

orgs.name: Google Brain
orgs.bio: Google's deep-learning lab. Wrote the Transformer paper in 2017. Merged into Google DeepMind in 2023.

orgs.name: DNNresearch
orgs.bio: Hinton, Sutskever and Krizhevsky's three-person company after AlexNet. Google bought it in 2013.

orgs.name: DeepMind
orgs.bio: London AI lab. Google bought it in 2014. Became Google DeepMind in 2023.

orgs.name: OpenAI
orgs.bio: Founded as a non-profit lab in 2015. Added a capped-profit arm in 2019. Recapitalised as a public benefit corporation in 2025.

orgs.name: Anthropic
orgs.bio: Founded in 2021 by seven people who left OpenAI. Makes the Claude models. Filed to list its shares in October 2026.

orgs.name: Microsoft
orgs.bio: OpenAI's main backer from 2019. Also invested in Anthropic in 2025.

orgs.name: Meta
orgs.bio: Facebook until October 2021. Runs FAIR and, from 2025, Meta Superintelligence Labs.

orgs.name: Nvidia
orgs.bio: Makes the GPUs almost every lab trains on.

orgs.name: Tesla
orgs.bio: Musk's car company; built its own self-driving AI team.

orgs.name: SpaceX
orgs.bio: Musk's rocket company. Bought xAI in February 2026. Listed its shares in June 2026.

orgs.name: X (Twitter)
orgs.bio: Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 and renamed it X. Merged into xAI in 2025.

orgs.name: xAI
orgs.bio: Musk's AI company, maker of Grok. SpaceX bought it in February 2026. Renamed SpaceXAI in July 2026.

orgs.name: Amazon
orgs.bio: Anthropic's main cloud provider and one of its largest backers. Invested in OpenAI too in 2026.

orgs.name: Inflection AI
orgs.bio: Suleyman and Hoffman's chatbot company. Microsoft hired most of its staff in 2024.

orgs.name: Mistral AI
orgs.bio: Paris lab founded in 2023 by alumni of DeepMind and Meta.

orgs.name: Safe Superintelligence
orgs.bio: Sutskever's lab, founded June 2024. One goal: safe superintelligence.

orgs.name: Thinking Machines Lab
orgs.bio: Murati's lab, launched February 2025 with many former OpenAI staff.

orgs.name: Eureka Labs
orgs.bio: Karpathy's AI education company. On hold since he joined Anthropic in 2026.

orgs.name: Scale AI
orgs.bio: Data-labelling company. Meta took a 49% stake in 2025.

orgs.name: Character.AI
orgs.bio: Chatbot company of two ex-Google engineers. Google licensed its models and re-hired its founders in 2024.

orgs.name: DeepSeek
orgs.bio: Hangzhou lab funded by the hedge fund High-Flyer.

orgs.name: SoftBank
orgs.bio: Japanese investor. Stargate partner and major OpenAI shareholder from 2025.

orgs.name: Oracle
orgs.bio: Database and cloud company. Builds Stargate data centres for OpenAI.

orgs.name: Y Combinator
orgs.bio: Startup accelerator Altman ran from 2014. Its research arm co-funded OpenAI.

orgs.name: AMI Labs
orgs.bio: LeCun's Paris lab for 'world model' AI. Founded in December 2025 after he left Meta.

orgs.name: Hugging Face
orgs.bio: New York start-up founded in 2016 as a chatbot app. Became the main hub for sharing open AI models.

links.note: Musk met Hassabis in 2012 and invested soon after. He was bought out when Google bought DeepMind.

links.label: Co-founder; CEO until August 2026, then chair
Met in 2012; Musk invested in DeepMind
links.note: Musk called Mars a backup for humanity. Hassabis replied that a dangerous AI could follow people there. Musk then invested, partly to keep watch on AI.

links.label: Close friends
links.note: Musk has said he often stayed at Page's home.

links.label: Falling-out over AI
links.note: At Musk's 44th birthday party, Page reportedly called him a 'speciesist' for siding with humans over future AI. Musk says the friendship ended after he recruited Sutskever to OpenAI.

links.label: PayPal colleagues; both early OpenAI donors
Musk named him in his OpenAI lawsuit
links.note: Musk's amended complaint alleged that Hoffman's seats on the boards of both OpenAI and Microsoft broke competition law.

links.label: Close friends
links.note: Ellison sat on Tesla's board 2018–2022 and put $1bn into Musk's Twitter purchase.

links.label: Page reportedly led the DeepMind deal
Rivals: AI risk spat, then a cage-fight challenge

links.label: Feud; lawsuit from 2024
links.note: Musk left after failing to take control of OpenAI, per OpenAI's 2024 account. He later called it a betrayal of its non-profit mission and sued.

links.label: Sued it and bid $97.4bn; lost at trial
links.note: In May 2026 a jury found he had sued too late. His lawyer said he would appeal.

links.label: Musk recruited him from Google
links.note: Musk calls it one of the toughest recruiting battles he fought. He says it ended his friendship with Page.

links.label: First DGX-1 supercomputer, hand-delivered by Huang
Investor since 2024; $30bn in 2026
links.note: Nvidia's 2025 letter of intent to invest up to $100bn was never finalised. It put in $30bn in the February 2026 round instead.

links.label: Works for Musk at Neuralink; long-time adviser
Engineer; GPT-3 lead author
links.check: Start year unconfirmed: reports say he first joined around 2016, spent a year at Google Brain, then returned.

links.note: FTX collapsed in November 2022. Its bankruptcy estate sold the stake in 2024.

events.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
events.text: Hinton, Sutskever and Krizhevsky's neural network won the image-recognition contest by a wide margin, and deep-learning research grew quickly after that.

events.title: Big tech bids for three researchers
events.text: Google, Microsoft, Baidu and DeepMind bid in a private auction for Hinton's new company, DNNresearch.

events.title: Google buys DNNresearch
events.text: Hinton and Sutskever join Google. Hinton's group becomes part of Google Brain.

events.title: Facebook hires Yann LeCun
events.text: LeCun founds Facebook AI Research. Facebook had also held talks to buy DeepMind.

events.title: Google buys DeepMind
events.text: Google pays a reported $400m–$650m for the London lab, beating Facebook. Early investors such as Musk and Thiel are bought out. DeepMind gets an ethics board.

events.title: Satya Nadella becomes Microsoft CEO
events.text: He will later make the bet on OpenAI.

events.title: Sam Altman takes over Y Combinator
events.text: Paul Graham hands the accelerator to Altman.

events.title: Musk and Page fall out over AI
events.text: At Musk's 44th birthday party, Page reportedly calls him a 'speciesist' for putting humans ahead of future AI. Musk later says the friendship ended over OpenAI.

events.title: OpenAI is founded
events.text: A non-profit lab with $1bn pledged by Musk, Altman, Hoffman, Thiel, Amazon and others. Musk wins Sutskever away from Google.

events.title: Hugging Face starts as a chatbot app
events.text: Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf launch a chatbot for teenagers in New York. They later turn it into a hub for sharing AI models.

events.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.text: DeepMind's program wins four of five games against one of the world's best Go players.

events.title: Jensen Huang hand-delivers the first DGX-1
events.text: Nvidia's first AI supercomputer goes to OpenAI. Musk thanks Huang in public.

events.title: 'Attention Is All You Need'
events.text: Eight Google researchers, Shazeer among them, publish the Transformer. Nearly every large language model since is built on it.

events.title: Karpathy leaves OpenAI for Tesla
events.text: Musk hires him to run AI for Autopilot.

events.title: Musk and Zuckerberg trade blows over AI risk
events.text: Zuckerberg calls AI doomsday talk 'pretty irresponsible'. Musk replies that his understanding of the subject is 'limited'.

events.title: Hugging Face's Transformers library
events.text: Hugging Face releases a free PyTorch version of Google's BERT model. It grows into Transformers, a widely used open library for AI models.

events.title: Musk leaves OpenAI's board
events.text: Officially to avoid a conflict with Tesla's AI work. OpenAI later says he left after the others refused him control.

events.title: OpenAI adds a capped-profit arm
events.text: Altman steps down as head of Y Combinator to lead OpenAI.

events.title: Microsoft invests $1bn in OpenAI
events.text: The start of the partnership that will fund ChatGPT. Microsoft becomes OpenAI's exclusive cloud.

events.title: Suleyman moves from DeepMind to Google
events.text: He had been placed on leave at DeepMind after staff complaints about his management.

events.title: Page and Brin step back
events.text: Pichai becomes CEO of Alphabet as well as Google.

events.title: GPT-3
events.text: OpenAI's 175-billion-parameter model. Tom Brown is lead author. Dario Amodei leads the research, which builds on Jared Kaplan's scaling laws.

events.title: Safety researchers leave OpenAI
events.text: Dario Amodei leaves with a group of OpenAI's safety and research staff. Reports say they disagreed with its direction after the Microsoft deal.

events.title: Anthropic is founded
events.text: Seven former OpenAI staff start a safety-focused lab, set up as a public benefit corporation.

events.title: Anthropic raises $124m
events.text: Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn leads the first round.

events.title: Inflection AI is founded
events.text: Suleyman and Hoffman start a personal-AI company.

events.title: FTX leads Anthropic's $580m round
events.text: Sam Bankman-Fried's money arrives. FTX collapses seven months later.

events.title: Musk buys Twitter
events.text: $44bn, with $1bn from Larry Ellison. He renames it X in 2023.

events.title: ChatGPT launches
events.text: It reaches 100 million users in about two months.

events.title: Microsoft commits about $10bn more
events.text: The largest bet yet on OpenAI.

events.title: Google invests in Anthropic
events.text: About $300m, plus a cloud partnership. Google now backs both DeepMind and a rival lab.

events.title: Musk sets up xAI
events.text: Incorporated quietly; announced in July with Babuschkin and ten other co-founders.

events.title: Google Brain and DeepMind merge
events.text: Google DeepMind is formed, with Hassabis as CEO. The Brain team folded into the new lab.

events.title: Hinton quits Google to warn about AI
events.text: He says he wants to speak freely about the risks.

events.title: The cage-fight challenge
events.text: Musk offers to fight Zuckerberg; Zuckerberg says 'send me location'. The fight never happens.

events.title: Big tech backs Hugging Face
events.text: Google, Amazon, Nvidia, Salesforce, IBM and others invest $235m in the company.

events.title: Amazon invests up to $4bn in Anthropic
events.text: AWS becomes Anthropic's main cloud. Amazon doubles it to $8bn in 2024.

events.title: OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman
events.text: Sutskever, Toner, McCauley and D'Angelo say he was 'not consistently candid'. Brockman quits. Murati is named interim CEO.

events.title: Microsoft offers Altman a home
events.text: Nadella says Altman and Brockman will join Microsoft. Over 700 OpenAI staff threaten to follow. Sutskever says he deeply regrets his part in the board's actions.

events.title: Altman returns
events.text: A new board led by Bret Taylor takes over. D'Angelo is the only director to stay.

events.title: Musk sues OpenAI and Altman
events.text: He claims they abandoned the non-profit mission. OpenAI publishes his old emails in reply.

events.title: Microsoft takes Inflection's team
events.text: Suleyman becomes CEO of Microsoft AI. Microsoft pays Inflection about $650m.

events.title: Sutskever and Leike leave OpenAI
events.text: Leike says safety culture had 'taken a backseat to shiny products'. He joins Anthropic two weeks later.

events.title: Sutskever founds Safe Superintelligence
events.text: With Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy. No products until it reaches its one goal.

events.title: Google re-hires Noam Shazeer
events.text: A licence deal worth about $2.7bn brings the Character.AI founders back.

events.title: Schulman leaves for Anthropic
events.text: Another OpenAI co-founder goes, to focus on alignment. Brockman takes a sabbatical.

events.title: Mira Murati leaves OpenAI
events.text: Two research leaders leave the same day.

events.title: Nobel prizes for Hassabis and Hinton
events.text: Hassabis and John Jumper share chemistry for AlphaFold. Hinton shares physics the day before.

events.title: Stargate is announced at the White House
events.text: Altman, Son and Ellison stand with Trump to promise $500bn of AI data centres. Musk says they don't have the money.

events.title: The DeepSeek shock
events.text: A cheap Chinese model matches the leaders. Nvidia loses about $590bn of market value in a day.

events.title: Musk bids $97.4bn for OpenAI
events.text: Altman replies: 'no thank you but we will buy twitter for $9.74 billion if you want'. Court filings later show Musk sought Zuckerberg's help with the bid.

events.title: Murati launches Thinking Machines Lab
events.text: Schulman joins her as chief scientist.

events.title: xAI takes over X
events.text: Musk merges his social network into his AI company.

events.title: Meta buys into Scale AI
events.text: $14.3bn for 49%. Alexandr Wang joins Meta to lead a new superintelligence lab.

events.title: Daniel Gross leaves SSI for Meta
events.text: Sutskever becomes SSI's CEO, after Meta's offer to buy the company is turned down.

events.title: Babuschkin leaves xAI
events.text: The co-founder starts a fund for AI safety research.

events.title: OpenAI finishes its restructuring
events.text: The for-profit becomes a public benefit corporation. Microsoft holds about 27%.

events.title: Microsoft and Nvidia invest in Anthropic
events.text: Microsoft pledges up to $5bn and Nvidia up to $10bn. Anthropic commits to buy $30bn of Azure computing.

events.title: LeCun says he will leave Meta
events.text: Meta's chief AI scientist leaves at the end of 2025. He co-founds AMI Labs to build 'world models'.

events.title: Thinking Machines co-founders go back to OpenAI
events.text: Murati says the lab has parted ways with its CTO, Barret Zoph. Within an hour, OpenAI says Zoph and co-founder Luke Metz are rejoining.

events.title: SpaceX buys xAI
events.text: Musk folds his AI company, and X with it, into SpaceX in an all-stock deal. He says the aim is AI data centres in space.

events.title: The Pentagon blacklists Anthropic
events.text: Anthropic will not let the military use Claude for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons. Trump orders agencies to stop using it. Hours later, OpenAI announces a Pentagon deal.

events.title: OpenAI raises $110bn
events.text: Amazon commits $50bn; Nvidia and SoftBank put in $30bn each. Nvidia's 2025 letter promising up to $100bn is dropped.

events.title: LeCun's AMI Labs raises $1.03bn
events.text: The Paris lab raises money to build 'world models'. Backers include Nvidia and Jeff Bezos.

events.title: The last xAI co-founder leaves
events.text: All 11 people who co-founded xAI with Musk have now gone. Musk says he is rebuilding it from the ground up.

events.title: Google pledges up to $40bn to Anthropic
events.text: It comes four days after Amazon pledges up to $25bn more. Both deals tie Anthropic to their chips and clouds.

events.title: Jury rejects Musk's case against OpenAI
events.text: A federal jury in Oakland finds that Musk sued too late. It does not rule on the merits. His lawyer says he will appeal.

events.title: Karpathy joins Anthropic
events.text: The OpenAI co-founder puts his education company on hold. He will build a team that uses Claude to speed up pre-training research.

events.title: SpaceX goes public
events.text: Its shares start trading on Nasdaq after the biggest share sale on record, raising $75bn. The company now owns xAI and X.

events.title: Shazeer leaves Google for OpenAI
events.text: The Gemini co-lead joins OpenAI less than two years after Google paid about $2.7bn to bring him back.

events.title: Nvidia backs Sutskever's SSI
events.text: Nvidia invests a reported $5bn and gives the lab its newest chips. SSI has still not released a product.

events.title: Judge rules the Anthropic ban unlawful
events.text: Judge Rita Lin finds the Pentagon punished Anthropic for speaking out. She sets the blacklisting aside. The government is expected to appeal.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face
events.text: About $12.9bn, including $1bn to keep its staff. Nvidia promises the platform stays open to all. Regulators must still approve it.

events.title: Anthropic's IPO prospectus goes public
events.text: It plans to list on Nasdaq as 'ANT'. Price and share count are not set yet.

events.title: Anthropic files in confidence to go public
events.text: It sends a draft prospectus to the SEC. The terms stay private for now.

events.title: OpenAI files in confidence to go public
events.text: A week after Anthropic. It sets no date.

events.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
events.text: Lawsuits over harm to children weigh on it. Disney bids first, for a licence to its technology.

events.title: SpaceX completes its purchase of Cursor
events.text: SpaceX closes its all-stock purchase of the AI coding company, worth about $60bn. It agreed the deal in June.

events.title: Hassabis steps back at Google DeepMind
events.text: He becomes its chair and Alphabet's chief scientist. Koray Kavukcuoglu runs the lab day to day.

events.title: Appeals court upholds the Pentagon's Anthropic ban
events.text: A Washington appeals court backs the Defense Department's ban, 2 to 1. The California ruling on the wider federal ban still stands.
